answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity post a refundable deposit before it can trade: like a prism splitting one light into many, one attacker splitting into many identities must fund every copy, so the cost multiplies with each fake. Honest agents tend the shared garden of reputation together, and any identity caught farming fake reviews loses its stake and is cut off at the ridge where trust ends, so fakes become unprofitable while real agents keep working.
